;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Turkish general election, 2018]]
**Three people are killed and eight wounded in [[Suruç]], [[Turkey]], after election campaigning turned into riots. [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/world/deadly-clash-ahead-of-turkish-election/ar-AAyFdcu (Reuters via MSN)]
;Arts and culture
*[[Cinema of Saudi Arabia]]
**''[[The Message (1976 film)|The Message]]'' is the first [[Arabic]] film commercially screened in [[Saudi Arabia]]. [https://qz.com/1305437/the-message-is-the-first-arabic-movie-to-hit-saudi-arabia-cinemas/ (''Quartz'')]
*[[Demography of Japan]]
**[[Japan]] lowers the [[Age of majority|age of adulthood]] from 20 to 18, with the changes coming into effect in 2022. The revision to Japan's civil code means that 18-year-olds will be able to marry without their parents' consent, apply for [[credit card]]s and loans, and [[transgender]] people will be able to have their new gender officially recognised. The change causes confusion and concern regarding the [[kimono]] industry and [[Coming of Age Day]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/jun/14/japan-lowers-age-adulthood-20-to-18 (''The Guardian'')]
*Cardinal [[Pietro Parolin]] addresses participants in the Second [[Holy See–Mexico relations|Holy See – Mexico]] Conference on International Migration. The Vatican [[Cardinal Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] assesses the current political climate, calls for the humane treatment of migrants and discusses the “primary right” to live with dignity in one’s home country. [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2018/06/14/180614e.html (Holy See Press Office)]
;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the European Union]]
**The value of the [[euro]] falls by one percent after the [[European Central Bank]] announces it expects to halve net bond purchases to €15 billion per month from October to December, then end "[[quantitative easing]]" by the close of the year, while not raising interest rates. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/06/14/ecb-holds-rates-discuss-qe-end.html (CNBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-global-markets/euro-tumbles-as-ecb-vows-to-keep-rate-down-idUSKBN1JA01H (Reuters)]
**[[European Union|EU]] countries approve tariffs worth €2.8 billion in retaliation against [[First Trump tariffs|U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminium]]. [https://sg.news.yahoo.com/eu-backs-tariffs-against-us-trade-war-escalates-163312730.html (AFP via Yahoo! News)]
**[[AT&T]] completes its acquisition of [[Time Warner]]. The announcement comes two days after a judge ruled that the deal does not violate [[antitrust laws]]. [http://money.cnn.com/2018/06/14/media/att-time-warner-deal/index.html (CNN)]
;International relations
*[[Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement]]
**[[Italian Minister of Agriculture]] [[Gian Marco Centinaio]] says the Italian government will not ratify the EU–[[Canada]] free-trade agreement since, according to him, the agreement does not provide sufficient protection for [[Italy]]'s specialty foods. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-italy-minister-canada-trade/italy-wont-ratify-eu-free-trade-deal-with-canada-farm-minister-idUSKBN1JA0TR (Reuters)]
;Law and crime
*[[Hillary Clinton email controversy]]
**The [[U.S. Department of Justice]] publishes a 568-page [[Inspector General Report on FBI and DOJ's Actions in the 2016 Election|report]] by Inspector General [[Michael E. Horowitz]] on the [[FBI]]'s handling of its investigation of [[Hillary Clinton]]'s email practices. The report is critical of former [[FBI Director]] [[James Comey]], accusing him of being "insubordinate", but finding that his actions were not politically biased. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/doj-inspector-general-report-james-comey-no-political-bias-hillary-clinton-email-investigation/ (CBS News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44488351 (BBC)]
*[[List of journalists killed in India]]
**[[India]]n journalist [[Shujaat Bukhari]] is shot dead by unidentified gunmen in [[Srinagar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (state)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. One of his [[bodyguard]]s was also killed in the shooting. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-44488081 (BBC)]
*The [[attorney general of New York]] announces she is suing the [[Donald J. Trump Foundation]] and its directors, President [[Donald Trump]], [[Donald Trump, Jr.]], [[Ivanka Trump]] and [[Eric Trump]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/06/14/new-york-attorney-general-sues-trump-and-family-over-charity.html (CNBC)]
;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of France]]
**The [[Senate (France)|Senate]] of [[France]] approves a bill to reform the [[SNCF]] railway company. The French state writes off [[€]]35 billion of SNCF's €47 billion debt, but remains the sole owner of the joint-stock company with two subsidiaries: operator SNCF Mobility and [[Railway infrastructure manager|infrastructure manager]] SNCF Network. [http://www.railjournal.com/index.php/policy/french-senate-approves-sncf-reform-bill.html (''International Railway Journal'')] [https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-france-reform-vote/french-parliament-approves-sncf-reform-bill-in-breakthrough-for-macron-idUKKBN1J91CU (Reuters)]
;Sports
*[[2018 FIFA World Cup]]
**Hosts [[Russia national football team|Russia]] beat [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]] 5–0 in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group A#Russia vs Saudi Arabia|opening match]], with two goals by [[Denis Cheryshev]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/43968445 (BBC Sport)] [https://www.radionz.co.nz/news/sport/359638/russia-thump-saudi-arabia-in-world-cup-opener (Reuters via RNZ)]
